blocks.x: A tight market

[CBRE's 2026 outlook](https://www.cbre.com/insights/articles/whats-ahead-for-winnipeg-commercial-real-estate-in-2026) put Winnipeg industrial vacancy around 3.5% in January 2026. [CBRE's Q3 2026 figures](https://mktgdocs.cbre.com/2299/85cf799d-8904-4d62-841f-540174867002-2006882353/Winnipeg_Industrial_Figures_Q3.pdf) put Winnipeg industrial availability, a different measure, at 3.1%, or 2.8% within city limits. That is well below the [5.2% national rate CBRE reports](https://www.cbre.com/insights/figures/canada-industrial-figures-q3-2026).

[The Q3 figures](https://www.cbre.com/insights/figures/winnipeg-industrial-figures-q3-2026) also reported about 493,000 square feet under construction, with the Southwest and Northwest submarkets leading the tightening.
New buildings take time to plan and build, and they lease at higher rents. Demand is strongest for modern space, so older buildings need to be reliable to compete.
Why older industrial buildings in Winnipeg need attention
Many older industrial buildings are concrete block or brick, built decades ago. They face common issues:
**Cracked or spalling masonry** from years of freeze-thaw cycles.
**Failed mortar joints** that let water into walls.
**Deteriorated parging** at foundation level.
**Old overhead and man doors** that leak air and are hard to secure.
**Damaged or inefficient windows.**
Left alone, these problems get worse. Water in masonry freezes and expands, causing more damage each winter. Interior damage can follow, affecting tenants and inventory.
Our view: protect the envelope, protect the rent

In a tight market, older buildings can still compete, but only if tenants see them as reliable. A building with visible cracks, leaks or failing doors invites tenant complaints, higher maintenance costs and, eventually, vacancy.

Beyond masonry
Once the envelope is sound, other upgrades can improve tenant appeal:
**Doors:** new insulated man doors and better-sealing entries improve security and comfort.
**Office areas:** many industrial tenants need upgraded front offices, with new flooring, paint and layouts.
**Interior demolition:** removing outdated offices or partitions to open space.
**Painting:** exterior and interior painting refreshes the building and protects surfaces.
Timing

Masonry work is weather-sensitive. Mortar needs suitable temperatures to cure, so most exterior masonry in Winnipeg happens between spring and fall. Owners who assess buildings now can plan and price work over the winter, then start as soon as conditions allow.
Questions to ask about your building

Owners of older industrial buildings should ask: When was the masonry last inspected? Are there areas of visible cracking, spalling or staining? Have tenants reported leaks or drafts? Are doors secure, insulated and in good working order? What will a tenant's inspector or a lender's assessor find?
The answers usually point to a short list of priorities. Addressing them protects the building, supports leasing and can help at refinancing.
What to watch

CBRE says the space under construction, most of it in the Southeast and Southwest submarkets, will help address the lack of modern, high-clearance space. As new space delivers, tenants will have more choice, and older buildings in poor condition may feel the competition first. Owners who invest in their envelopes now may be better placed when that happens.
Working around tenants

Industrial masonry work can often be done while tenants operate, but it needs planning. Contractors should coordinate access to loading areas and parking, schedule noisy work such as cutting and grinding around tenant operations, and protect vehicles, inventory and entrances from dust and debris.
Clear communication with tenants before and during the work helps avoid disputes and keep operations running. Phasing by elevation, one wall at a time, also limits disruption.
The bottom line

Winnipeg's tight industrial market gives older buildings a chance to compete, but only if they are kept in good condition. Commercial masonry services and envelope repairs are the foundation of that work, protecting both the building and its income. A vacancy caused by a leaking or failing building can cost more than the repair that would have prevented it.
